geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
The final covers the whole year. Use the targets below as a checklist: can you do each one without notes?

  • Unit 1 Seeing and Reasoning: Pictures and measurements suggest; only proof convinces.
  • Unit 2 Lines, Angles, and Constructions: A few postulates about rulers and protractors produce reliable theorems about angles.
  • Unit 3 Rigid Motions and Symmetry: Sliding, flipping, and turning keep shape and size.
  • Unit 4 Triangle Congruence: Three well-chosen parts are enough to pin down a triangle.
  • Unit 5 Inequalities and Parallel Lines: Some facts need no parallel postulate; the 180 degree angle sum does.
  • Unit 6 Quadrilaterals and Polygons: Quadrilaterals form a family tree defined by their properties.
  • Unit 7 Area, Pythagoras, and Coordinates: Area is preserved by cutting and rearranging, and that proves the Pythagorean Theorem.
  • Unit 8 Similarity and Dilations: Dilations change size but keep shape, so ratios are preserved.
  • Unit 9 Right Triangles and Trigonometry: In similar right triangles, side ratios depend only on the angle.
  • Unit 10 Circles and Concurrence: Angles and segments in circles follow hidden rules tied to arcs.
  • Unit 11 Regular Polygons and Circle Measure: A circle is the limit of regular polygons, and pi comes from that limit.
  • Unit 12 Solids and Design: Slices tell us about volume (Cavalieri), and geometry lets us design real objects.
